## 1 · The 30-second verdict

A contract-state reader that reads **4 typed values** from a live mainnet
contract — **every read is a Chain MCP `tools/call` by name**
(`get_chain_info`, `get_code`, `get_block_number`, `eth_call`) against the
hosted MCP at `https://mcp.pharos.xyz/mcp`. All values are pinned to a single
block, shown with raw hex, decoded values, human formatting (decimals read
from the contract itself), and address labels. Failure states fail loudly —
never silent zeros. **Zero raw JSON-RPC calls** against any RPC URL.

- **Contract:** USDC `0xc879c018db60520f4355c26ed1a6d572cdac1815`
  ([explorer](https://pharosscan.xyz/address/0xc879c018db60520f4355c26ed1a6d572cdac1815))
  — a real token real users hold, read on the chain the hosted MCP serves.
- **Chain:** Pharos mainnet, chain ID **1672** (asserted via MCP
  `get_chain_info` before every run).
- **MCP:** `pharos-mcp-server 0.1.0`, keyless Streamable HTTP
  (`initialize` → session header → `tools/call`).
- **Cost:** 0 PHRS — all reads are free; no deployment, no transactions.
- **Proof:** live transcript + per-run evidence manifest recording the MCP
  endpoint, tool names, pinned block, git commit and dirty flag.

## 2 · Requirements → evidence

| # | Official Arena requirement | How this submission meets it | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read ≥3 different values from one contract **via Chain MCP** | 4 values from one contract — `name()` (string), `symbol()` (string), `decimals()` (uint8), `totalSupply()` (uint256) — each read as an MCP `tools/call` named `eth_call`. No `eth_*` call is ever made against an RPC URL. | `bin/read-contract-state.py` (`read_view`); manifest `mcpToolsCalled`; `sample-output/transcript-live.txt` |
| 2 | Show contract address + block number read at | Every run prints the contract address and the pinned block; all 4 reads carry that block. | Transcript header; manifest `blockReadAt` |
| 3 | Format raw values for humans (decimals applied, addresses labelled) | `decimals()` is read **from the contract itself (6)** — never assumed — and `totalSupply` renders as `43,376,165.573737 USDC`. Addresses are checksummed and labelled via `config/labels.json`; the zero address is special-cased; unknown addresses print `unlabeled address` — never a made-up label. | Transcript `human` lines; `config/labels.json` |
| 4 | Short README (which contract, how to run, sample output) | This file: contract + explorer link (§1), one-command run (§4), real sample output (§5). | — |

## 3 · Which contract

USDC on Pharos mainnet (`0xc879c018db60520f4355c26ed1a6d572cdac1815`,
code length 1798 bytes, verified via MCP `get_code`). The hosted Chain MCP
serves mainnet (chain 1672) only, so the task reads where the MCP reads —
a production token instead of a test deployment.

| # | Value | Type | Selector |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `name` | `string` | `0x06fdde03` → `"USDC"` |
| 2 | `symbol` | `string` | `0x95d89b41` → `"USDC"` |
| 3 | `decimals` | `uint8` | `0x313ce567` → `6` |
| 4 | `totalSupply` | `uint256` | `0x18160ddd` → `43376165573737` raw → `43,376,165.573737 USDC` |

## 4 · How to run

Prerequisites: Python 3 + `requests` (stdlib otherwise). No API key, no
private key, no RPC URL — the Chain MCP is keyless. No install step.

```bash
# read everything, pretty-printed, with a per-run evidence manifest
bin/read-contract-state.sh --manifest evidence/run-manifest.json

# pin a historical block instead of latest
bin/read-contract-state.sh --block 20686000

# read a different contract (any mainnet address with code)
bin/read-contract-state.sh --contract 0x...

# negative-path suite (no-code address + unknown selector): both must fail loudly
bin/read-contract-state.sh --negative

# test suite: reader vs INDEPENDENT raw-JSON-RPC re-reads + gates
bash test/run-tests.sh
```

The script asserts **chain ID 1672 via MCP `get_chain_info` first** and aborts
on mismatch; checks the address holds bytecode via MCP `get_code`; pins one
block via MCP `get_block_number`; then issues all `eth_call`s at that block —
each one an MCP `tools/call` by name.

tasks.readme_markdown:
# T02 — Event/Log Monitor

**Live on Pharos mainnet (chain 1672), via the Chain MCP.** A persistent,
reorg-tolerant event monitor that issues **every chain read through the Chain MCP
tools `get_logs` / `get_block_number` by name** (`https://mcp.pharos.xyz/mcp`,
MCP Streamable HTTP, keyless) — no raw `eth_*` JSON-RPC anywhere in this task.
It watches real USDC `Transfer` events, decodes each into readable fields, never
duplicates, and survives a `kill -9` without re-emission.

> **Resubmission note (2026-10-19):** the first submission queried the Atlantic
> RPC directly and was returned with *"Switch to Chain MCP get_logs and
> resubmit."* This build does exactly that — on mainnet, which the reviewer
> explicitly allowed ("mainnet is fine"). All v1 Atlantic artifacts
> (`src/LogEmitter.sol`, `state.v1-atlantic.json`, `poll.v1-atlantic.log`,
> `alerts.v1-atlantic.jsonl`, `run.v1-atlantic.out`) are preserved in this
> folder for the record.

---

## 1. What it is

A Python monitor (`monitor.py`) watching USDC
`0xc879c018db60520f4355c26ed1a6d572cdac1815` on Pharos mainnet. It scans block
ranges with the **Chain MCP `get_logs` tool** (chunked ≤1,000 blocks per call —
the server-enforced cap), filters by address + topic0 (computed from the event
signature at runtime via keccak256 — never hardcoded), decodes into readable
fields (`from`, `to`, `value` in USDC), and appends alerts to `alerts.jsonl`
with block number, tx hash, and log index.

## 2. The target contract

USDC on Pharos mainnet — a token real users hold:

| | |
|---|---|
| Contract | `0xc879c018db60520f4355c26ed1a6d572cdac1815` |
| Event | `Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value)` |
| topic0 | `0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef` (computed at runtime, `monitor.py topics`) |
| Decimals | 6 (verified via MCP `eth_call` `decimals()`) |

Explorer: https://pharosscan.xyz/address/0xc879c018db60520f4355c26ed1a6d572cdac1815

## 3. How to run

No API key, no private key, no RPC URL — the Chain MCP is keyless:

```bash
cd tasks/t02-event-log-monitor

# print the topic0 signature (computed at runtime, never hardcoded)
python3 monitor.py topics

# continuous poller (8s cycles; cursor persists in state.json)
python3 monitor.py run

# deterministic test: scan a known range, assert the exact event count
python3 monitor.py test --from-block=20684347 --to-block=20685847 --expect-count=87
```

State files: `state.json` (chain_id + cursor + seen set), `poll.log`
(per-cycle log), `alerts.jsonl` (decoded alerts).

## 4. Sample output (real run, 2026-10-19)

```
$ python3 monitor.py test --from-block=20684347 --to-block=20685847 --expect-count=87
connected: chain-mcp @ https://mcp.pharos.xyz/mcp (chain 1672)
scanned blocks 20684347..20685847 via chain-mcp:get_logs: found 87 Transfer event(s)
  Transfer block=20684351 tx=0x53f596fa1a934e3b5d74aedab6be138570c28ee93fe5e633b254ba1cbf23db1e logIndex=0x0 from=0x912c9ade24d44d8922f086d8dcb079f1363f647 to=0x936564245b69f5a293b42cbd752e0ee3bb68b470 value=157.463529 USDC
  Transfer block=20684416 tx=0xa61fd3c1ee1dd802b158ad215c8f3950fe75cdf10efec0bb49e217a77bba1a5a logIndex=0x1 from=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 to=0x2166d3a311a848d7713b6ef7a46e70f75d36fd67 value=22000.000000 USDC
  ... and 77 more
determinism check: re-scan returned the identical 87 event(s)
TEST PASS: exactly 87 Transfer event(s) in range
```

Every read in that run was a `get_logs` **tool call on the Chain MCP** —
1,501 blocks scanned in 2 chunked calls (≤1,000 blocks each, the server cap).

## 5. Continuous-operation evidence (mainnet, 2026-10-19)

- The poller ran 5-second cycles against `chain-mcp:get_logs`, logging every
  cycle to `poll.log`.
- **Live catch:** 18 real mainnet USDC Transfers were caught **while the poller
  was running** — each decoded (`from`/`to`/`value_usdc`) in the next cycle,
  e.g. block 20687008 tx
  `0x11ec559e5bef8165df872da5a86bfb549b3e837befe0435386b1f4543130c8b9`
  (19.998000 USDC; the same tx also carried a burn leg to `0x0000…0000`).
  Explorer: https://pharosscan.xyz/tx/0x11ec559e5bef8165df872da5a86bfb549b3e837befe0435386b1f4543130c8b9
- **Kill-9 test:** the poller was killed with `kill -9` mid-run and restarted.
  The cursor was restored exactly (20687108) from `state.json` (atomic write
  before every alert): **0 re-emissions** of the 13 pre-kill alerts, and 5
  genuinely new alerts were caught in the cycles after restart.
  Pre-kill alerts archived in `proof/alerts.pre-kill.jsonl`; poller logs in
  `proof/live-demo.out` / `proof/live-demo2.out`.

## 6. Design decisions

- **Chain MCP tools by name** — `get_block_number` for the tip, `get_logs` for
  every scan. The MCP session handshake (initialize → session id →
  `Mcp-Session-Id` header) is implemented in `ChainMCP`; a lost session
  re-handshakes once and retries.
- **Chunked get_logs (≤1,000 blocks/call)** — the MCP server enforces the cap
  (`Block range too large` past 1,000); the scanner chunks client-side too.
- **Dedupe by `blockNumber:logIndex`** — survives overlapping scans and restarts.
- **Persist-before-emit** — state.json is written (atomically, via tmp+rename)
  before any alert is emitted; a crash can never cause a duplicate alert or a
  skipped block.
- **2-block confirmation lag** — reorg tolerance; only confirmed blocks are scanned.
- **topic0 computed in code** (keccak256 via pycryptodome, byte-equal to the
  canonical `0xddf252ad…`) — no hardcoded hashes to drift.
- **Zero spend** — the hosted Chain MCP is keyless; reads cost nothing and need
  no wallet.

# What is the Pharos Chain MCP and which read tools does it expose for an AI agent?

The **Pharos Chain MCP** is a public Model Context Protocol server that lets AI agents query Pharos chain data and perform on-chain operations through MCP-compatible clients. Its hosted endpoint is `https://mcp.pharos.xyz/mcp`; it requires no API key and connects to chain ID `1672` (`0x688`). See [Pharos MCP](/tooling-and-infrastructure/mcp.md).

Its read and query tools are:

* **Chain and blocks:** `get_chain_info`, `get_block_number`, `get_block`, `get_gas_price`
* **Accounts and transactions:** `get_balance` (native PROS), `get_transaction_count`, `get_transaction`, `get_transaction_receipt`
* **Contracts and events:** `eth_call` (read-only contract calls), `get_code`, `get_storage_at`, `get_logs`
* **Gas estimation:** `estimate_gas` estimates gas without sending a transaction.

`send_raw_transaction` is also exposed, but it broadcasts a signed transaction rather than reading data. The hosted service allows 120 requests per minute per IP.

different surface that composes Chain MCP + docs). It is docs-only: it cannot
read chain state. The `sendFeedback` tool is deliberately never invoked (it files
a real report to the Pharos docs team).

### Requirements → evidence

| # | Official requirement (T04, Easy) | How it is met | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accepts NL question as input (`pharos-docs "how do I deploy a contract?"`) | `./pharos-docs` executable; question → live `searchDocumentation` call | README §4; `evidence/evidence.json` E1,E2,E3,E7,E8,M1,M2 |
| 2 | Returns concise answer + links/references to source doc sections | Answer cards: verbatim excerpts + `Source: <doc URL> (via Docs MCP, retrieved <date>)` | `evidence/evidence.json` citations |
| 3 | 'No good answer found' handled gracefully, never invents | UNVERIFIED miss path, exit code 2; relevance gate; closest-pages suggestions (labeled as browse hints, not answers) | `evidence/evidence.json` M1–M2; tests |
| 4 | README with install/usage + 3 example queries with outputs | This README: §3 install, §4 usage, §6 examples (all real MCP output) | Below |

**Machine-checked citations:** every quoted excerpt in the evidence battery is
asserted — offline — to be a verbatim substring of the raw MCP response it came
from (`evidence/raw/<id>.txt`). See `tests/test_cli.py::TestMachineCheck`.

## 2. Install

Requirements: Python 3.8+ (stdlib only — no pip packages), internet access
(every query calls the live Docs MCP).

```bash
cd tasks/t04-doc-search-cli
chmod +x pharos-docs
./pharos-docs "how do I deploy a contract?"
```

Run the test suite:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests.test_cli          # offline machine-checks (no network)
T04_LIVE=1 python3 -m unittest tests.test_cli.Live   # live MCP round-trips
```

Replay the evidence battery (real MCP calls; slow — the endpoint drops
connections and the client retries with backoff):

```bash
python3 evidence/run_evidence.py
```

## 3. Usage

```
pharos-docs "natural language question"
pharos-docs --json "question"          # machine-readable output
pharos-docs --top 5 "question"         # up to 5 answer cards
pharos-docs --page <doc-url>           # full page text via the getPage tool
pharos-docs --ask "question"           # synthesized answer via askQuestion
pharos-docs --raw-log <path> "q"       # also dump the raw MCP response text
```

Exit codes: `0` = DOC-GROUNDED answer, `2` = UNVERIFIED (no good answer found,
nothing invented), `1` = error (e.g. MCP unreachable after retries).

## 4. How it works

```
question
  → searchDocumentation tool @ docs.pharos.xyz/~gitbook/mcp
  → parse "Title / Link / Content" results
  → relevance gate: a result COVERS the question only if the question's
    distinctive terms (len ≥ 3, non-generic) appear in its title+content;
    all LONG terms (≥ 6 chars) must be present, plus ≥ half of all terms.
    (searchDocumentation always returns ~10 results, even for out-of-scope
    questions -- the gate is what makes "no" possible.)
  → top covering results become answer cards: verbatim excerpt windows
    around the densest cluster of question terms + doc URL + date
  → no covering result → UNVERIFIED (exit 2) + closest-pages browse hints
```

client (`src/docs_mcp.py`) retries with exponential backoff + jitter and
salvages partial SSE bodies. No `initialize` handshake is needed — the server
accepts `tools/call` statelessly.

tasks.readme_markdown:
*The keeper's hand stays the lamp it cannot vouch for — every transfer passes
the gate, or it does not pass at all.*

---

## 1 · What this is

A **policy gate that intercepts proposed transfers and BLOCKS any write that
breaches configured thresholds**. It is not a demo of a guardian — it *is*
the guardian that signed this task's only broadcast. A proposal enters;
six independent conditions are read live from the chain; a decision trace
is emitted; and only `ALLOW` reaches `cast send` — under a nonce lock, once,
with a receipt. `BLOCK` and `REFUSE` never broadcast. `REFUSE` is reserved
for mainnet-class actions, which this guardian declines outright, with no
override flag.

## 2 · The 4 mandatory Write Operation Pre-checks

Per the SkillEngine skill (`~/workspace/custom-skills/pharos-skill-engine/SKILL.md`,
"Write Operation Pre-checks"), implemented as pipeline conditions:

| # | Skill pre-check | Guardian condition | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Private key check | `key-present` | env `DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY` set; value never printed/logged |
| 2 | Derive public address, confirm | `sender-binding` | `cast wallet address` must derive to `policy.sender`; proposal sender must match |
| 3 | Network confirmation | `network` | `eth_chainId` read live; anything but 688689 ⇒ refused. Mainnet ⇒ REFUSE even with explicit re-confirmation (`policy.mainnet.enabled=false` is a hard firewall) |
| 4 | Automatic balance check | `balance` | `eth_getBalance` ≥ value + worst-case fee reserve; fail-closed on stale data |

Plus T05's own: **threshold** (per-tx + rolling-window caps) and **gas-price
sanity** (`eth_gasPrice` ≤ policy cap) — six conditions total, every one
configurable in `policy.yaml`.

## 3 · The policy file

One file, plain words, every number commented — `policy.yaml`:

```yaml
sender: "0xf76e6B0920e9332fF4410f6dD53F01722AbC71a3"
network:
  allowed_chain_id: 688689        # Atlantic testnet ONLY
  mainnet: { chain_id: 1672, enabled: false }   # listed only to be refused
limits:
  max_per_tx_phrs: "0.005"
  max_per_window_phrs: "0.02"
  window_minutes: 60
  max_gas_price_gwei: "50"
```

Nothing is hard-coded in `guardian.py`. Validate with
`python3 guardian.py validate`.

## 4 · How to run (both outcomes)

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH"
set -a; source ~/workspace/lightkeeper/.env; set +a

# HOLD — above threshold → BLOCKED, exit 2, no broadcast
python3 guardian.py propose --to 0xf76e6B0920e9332fF4410f6dD53F01722AbC71a3 --value-phrs 0.05

# FIRE — below threshold → APPROVED; `execute` broadcasts once (real tx)
python3 guardian.py execute --to 0xf76e6B0920e9332fF4410f6dD53F01722AbC71a3 --value-phrs 0.0001

# REFUSE — mainnet-class action → REFUSED, exit 3, no broadcast, no key use
python3 guardian.py propose --network mainnet --to 0xf76e6B0920e9332fF4410f6dD53F01722AbC71a3 --value-phrs 0.0001
```

Exit codes: `0` = ALLOW/success · `1` = error · `2` = BLOCK · `3` = REFUSE.
Audit trail: `run-logs/guardian-audit.jsonl` (one JSON line per evaluation).
Spend ledger: `run-logs/spend-ledger.jsonl` (feeds the rolling-window check).

## 5 · Evidence (real, on Atlantic testnet)

- **HOLD:** `run-logs/hold.log` — 0.05 PHRS proposal BLOCKED (`0.050000 PHRS >
  max_per_tx 0.005 PHRS`), exit 2, nothing broadcast, nothing spent.
- **FIRE:** `run-logs/fire.log` — 0.0001 PHRS self-transfer, 6/6 PASS →
  broadcast `0xe318dd0af236c292e6a1c21e0c98bd6088dac47fc24a8c0ad5d539912a23048c`,
  status 1, block 31481282 —
  https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0xe318dd0af236c292e6a1c21e0c98bd6088dac47fc24a8c0ad5d539912a23048c
- **WINDOW-LOAD ×4:** `run-logs/fire-window-{1..4}.log` — four 0.0045 PHRS
  dust fires, each ALLOW → broadcast, status 1 (blocks 31486305 / 31486321 /
  31486393 / 31486440):
  `0xb1ba9e2dc1c03e39d6896ecb07c063cf2a8b6a37712d47a321fae3213fd59a18`,
  `0x04effe58f393349714ff6a5badeff5780d2c30ccce238f8184075854eb223f3f`,
  `0xe160ca25fd76966a867fd36b761c08831ad54ed395069cfb59e1dc23ed912e7b`,
  `0xe51e3e9b7fb93d9232d092725eedd6aac6d6d8f3d1688e4def8bf9ad0d6e85c3`.
- **WINDOW-BLOCK:** `run-logs/window.log` — a fifth 0.0045 PHRS proposal
  passes per-tx (`0.0045 ≤ 0.005`) but the rolling window (0.018 + 0.0045 =
  0.0225 > 0.02) BLOCKS it, exit 2, nothing broadcast — the aggregate gate
  proven with a real on-chain ledger behind it.
- **REFUSE:** `run-logs/mainnet-refusal.log` — live `eth_chainId` read against
  the Pharos mainnet RPC returned 1672 → REFUSE, exit 3. Refused again with
  `--confirm-mainnet` supplied: refusal is unconditional.
- **Unit tests:** `python3 tests/test_policy_engine.py` — 13/13 pass (offline,
  mocked chain): boundary at threshold, rolling window, gas spike,
  insufficient balance, stale-data fail-closed, wrong-chain, mainnet refuse
  ±confirmation, missing key.
- **Spend:** 0.01915 PHRS total (0.0181 value + gas) of the 0.15 budget.
  See `evidence.json` for the machine-readable log.

## 6 · Security & honesty

tasks.readme_summary:
A multi-step on-chain workflow — **approve → lock → execute → settle** — driven by
agent code over receipt checks (`scripts/saga.py`). SkillEngine ships no native
retry and no rollback, so both are implemented here as explicit, unit-tested policy.
Two fixture contracts on Atlantic testnet (`TestToken`, `TestFixture`) play the
workflow's counterparty. Nothing is simulated: every step is a mined transaction,
every state transition is appended to a JSONL state log, and the failure run
contains a **real mined `status: 0`** receipt followed by **confirmed compensation
transactions** (refund + allowance revoke).

**Saga states:** `CREATED → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED | COMPENSATING → COMPENSATED | FAILED | COMPENSATION_FAILED`

**Step states:** `PENDING → PREPARED → BROADCAST → CONFIRMING → CONFIRMED | RETRYING → FAILED_PERMANENT`
tasks.readme_markdown:
One arm fails — the keeper does not drop the lamp;
it reaches back, and makes the sea whole again.

LIGHTKEEPER · T06 · Hard · 200 pts · SkillEngine · Atlantic testnet

--- ## 1. What this is A multi-step on-chain workflow — **approve → lock → execute → settle** — driven by agent code over receipt checks (`scripts/saga.py`). SkillEngine ships no native retry and no rollback, so both are implemented here as explicit, unit-tested policy. Two fixture contracts on Atlantic testnet (`TestToken`, `TestFixture`) play the workflow's counterparty. Nothing is simulated: every step is a mined transaction, every state transition is appended to a JSONL state log, and the failure run contains a **real mined `status: 0`** receipt followed by **confirmed compensation transactions** (refund + allowance revoke). ## 2. Architecture **Saga states:** `CREATED → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED | COMPENSATING → COMPENSATED | FAILED | COMPENSATION_FAILED` **Step states:** `PENDING → PREPARED → BROADCAST → CONFIRMING → CONFIRMED | RETRYING → FAILED_PERMANENT` - **Retry policy (agent code, not toolkit):** transient failures (dropped/missing receipt, RPC error) retry ≤3 times with 5/15/45s backoff and +20% gas bumps per attempt. A mined `0x0` is *permanent* — never retried, routed straight to compensation. Decision table unit-tested (`python3 scripts/saga.py --selftest`, 21 cases). - **Post-state gates:** a `0x1` receipt is not enough — each step also asserts on-chain state before the next starts (allowance ≥ amount, `locked` delta, `settled` flag, balance restoration). A gate failure escalates to compensation. - **Failure-broadcast mode** (opt-in, code-restricted): the forced-failure step bypasses the precheck and is sent with an explicit `--gas-limit` so `cast`'s client-side `eth_estimateGas` — which refuses to broadcast any reverting call — cannot swallow the failure before it reaches the chain. This is the only way to mine a genuine `0x0` through this toolchain, and it is documented, not hidden. ## 3. State log: `runs/t06-run-a-20261016-040851/state.log`. ## 4. Run B — forced failure → compensation (`COMPENSATED`) `runs/t06-run-b-20261016-042903/` · dust = 2000 wei LKTEST · approve(4000) leaves a real residual allowance so the revoke step is meaningful, not a no-op. | # | Step | Tx | Block | Status | Gas | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | approve(fixture, 4000) | [`0x452acae1…a928ba7`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0x452acae1ec4335ecd0842672c97383b5671e1ad950150224f307dcd17a928ba7) | 31482444 | ✅ 0x1 | 46,663 | | 2 | lock(2000) | [`0x0371814a…76f0eea`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0x0371814a1739f58698722db4915da1b718512c9bafcb347da3def4a6576f0eea) | 31482492 | ✅ 0x1 | 85,106 | | 3 | execute(minOut=2001) — **impossible** | [`0x91f7e021…f819b05`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0x91f7e02125434e3f29a56ed086f440a283ac000575fb1ff3369bbf269f819b05) | 31482534 | ❌ **0x0** | 24,231 | | C1 | compensate: refund() | [`0xe6cac311…fbb60ca`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0xe6cac3114397487f6d1b1efec721af968ee8868e196a9d5f6437d35b9fbb60ca) | 31482558 | ✅ 0x1 | 37,560 | | C2 | compensate: revoke approve(0) | [`0x0e807191…34759b`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0x0e80719119b7fb8781020e5a7fa0fcec01eeec167caa7329ac6781f1cb34759b) | 31482599 | ✅ 0x1 | 24,739 | The executor detected the `0x0` from the receipt, classified it permanent (no retry — one and only one attempt), transitioned `RUNNING → COMPENSATING`, and ran both compensations. tasks.readme_markdown:
---

## 1. What it is

A SkillEngine-style arbitrage scanner for Pharos Atlantic testnet. Each scan pins one block, reads **three independent on-chain AMM venues** in parallel, computes every directed cross-venue cycle with real constant-product math, nets **per-leg fees on notionals + slippage + gas**, and either **ACTs** (prepares — and, with `--execute`, broadcasts — the two-leg arb) or **SKIPs with a machine-readable reason**. Every scan, including failed ones, is appended to `scans.jsonl`.

The honesty strategy: testnet liquidity is thin, so the scanner is built to say *"no opportunity"* with the numbers rather than invent one. A truthful SKIP is a valid result; a fabricated spread is disqualifying.

## 2. How it works

Per scan: `blockNumber` → parallel `eth_call` `getReserves()` × 3 venues (one pinned block) → `eth_gasPrice` → `eth_estimateGas` per leg → economics over all 12 directed cycles (3 venues × 2 orders × 2 start tokens) → staleness check → threshold policy gate → append JSONL.

```
scan.py [--config config.json] [--out scans.jsonl] [--execute]
```

- Default run: read-only. Prints the full record, appends to `scans.jsonl`.
- `--execute`: only if decision is ACT — broadcasts the two prepared `swap` calls (dust, testnet), each `flock`-serialized, and records the tx hashes. On any broadcast failure the record is rewritten to `SKIP / EXECUTION_FAILED` with the stderr captured. Nothing is ever silently "pretended executed".

## 3. The venues (real, on-chain, independently readable)

No public DEX with usable liquidity exists on Atlantic for a test pair, so T07 deploys its own three minimal constant-product venues (`src/ArbPool.sol`, 0.30% fee/leg on the notional). Each is a separate contract with separate reserves — genuinely independent price sources, all executable:

| Venue | Address | Reserves (WPHRS / TKB) | Implied price |
|---|---|---|---|
| poolA | `0x8683C6D6EeAA57B03688f43Ad0cbCA0af26Cf464` | 1000 / 1000 | 1.0000 (reference) |
| poolB | `0x432BCd7bc6944Def44015bF00C82Eb50aA18A3F6` | 1000 / 980 | 0.9800 (WPHRS cheap → buy leg) |
| poolC | `0x3f0ae6f640f067B2532194a0ef2c869Aa49E587D` | 1000 / 1020 | 1.0200 (WPHRS dear → sell leg) |

Tokens: `WPHRS` (test wrapped native) `0x8a81455a477deeA986ca48cE83ca89C5331Da793`, `TKB` (test USD) `0x8BAa4fD0329dbf77c9fBFC44448B5669D356bfe1` — both `src/MockToken.sol`, minted by the deployer, no economic value.

## 4. The math (the figure T07 grades)

For each directed cycle, from the real reserves at the pinned block:

- **Quote:** `out = (amountIn·9970·rOut) / (rIn·10000 + amountIn·9970)` — identical integer math to the contract (cross-checked live in `test_math.py`).
- **Fees:** 30 bps **per leg on the notional** (`fee_leg1 = size·30/10000`, `fee_leg2 = leg1_out·30/10000`) — never on the spread.
- **Slippage:** quoted output vs the zero-fee constant-product ideal from the same reserves, per leg.
- **Gas:** `eth_estimateGas` for a representative swap × 2 legs × live `eth_gasPrice`, in PHRS.
- **Net:** `gross − gas`, all in WPHRS. `native_price_usd` is deliberately **null** in `config.json`: no USD price for PHRS is invented. WPHRS==PHRS 1:1 is documented test construction (deployer-minted), not a market price.

Skip reasons: `BELOW_THRESHOLD` · `STALE_QUOTE` (pinned block >50 behind tip) · `NO_LIQUIDITY` · `SOURCE_DOWN` · `NEGATIVE_NET` · `EXECUTION_FAILED`. Failed reads are errors, never zeros.

## 5. Running it

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH"
set -a; source ~/workspace/lightkeeper/.env; set +a   # ATLANTIC_RPC_URL
cd ~/workspace/lightkeeper/tasks/t07-arbitrage-scanner

python3 test_math.py            # 10 tests: pure math + live on-chain cross-check
python3 scanner.py              # read-only scan -> stdout + scans.jsonl
python3 scanner.py --execute    # ACT only: broadcasts the 2-leg arb (dust)
```

Dependencies: Python 3 stdlib only (`urllib`). No `web3`, no API keys.

## 6. Evidence

- `scans.jsonl` — every scan record (mode `LIVE`, pinned block, reserves, full cost decomposition, decision, tx hashes).
- `evidence.md` — full scan-run transcripts with real block numbers.
- `evidence.json` — every tx hash → `https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/<hash>`, spend log.
- `LINKS.md` — curl-verified links. `SUBMISSION.md` — copy-paste Arena pack.

Headline results (all on Atlantic, chain 688689):
- **Scan ACT** (pinned block 31482138, threshold 0.05 WPHRS): net **+0.138051195909437998 WPHRS** → executed leg1 `0x39fe2154…e2185de30`, leg2 `0xdcd894bb…ca380c58ad`, both status 1; deployer WPHRS balance 7000 → 7000.139809535909437998.
- **Scan SKIP / BELOW_THRESHOLD** (pinned 31482387, threshold 0.5 WPHRS): same real spread nets 0.138 < 0.5 → no broadcast, reason logged.
- **Scan SKIP / NEGATIVE_NET** (pinned 31482299): run right after our own arb consumed the spread — best route nets −0.253 WPHRS. The market responded; the scanner told the truth.

## 7. Honesty & limits

- Spreads come from real reserves; the venues are ours because no public Atlantic DEX offered readable test liquidity — stated openly in `REVIEWER_NOTES.md`.
- `forge script --broadcast` is **incompatible** with the Atlantic RPC (`PARAM_VERIFY_ERROR`); deployments used `forge create --broadcast` + `cast send` (same bytecode). The unused `script/DeployT07.s.sol` is kept for reference.
- One scan's `--execute` initially failed (`EXECUTION_FAILED`, missing `cast` on PATH) — the record is kept in `scans.jsonl` unedited, then the scan was re-run successfully. Append-only means append-only.
- Re-seeding a venue overwrites reserves via `seed()` (owner-only test function); inert leftover dust may sit in the pool but quotes always come from `getReserves()`.
- 28 workers share one deployer key: every broadcast is `flock /tmp/lk-nonce.lock`-serialized. Total T07-attributable spend is logged in `evidence.json` (≤ 0.15 PHRS budget).

tasks.readme_summary:
The Dry-Run Executor answers one question before any transaction is allowed near the chain: **what would happen if we sent this?** It simulates via `eth_call` + `estimateGas` — never broadcasting — and issues a signed-by-nobody **SimulationReceipt**: predicted PASS or FAIL, the exact revert reason on failure, the gas estimate with a **1.2× safety factor**, the predicted cost, and before/after state snapshots marked "chain unmodified".

Execution is **structurally gated**: the dry-run module cannot broadcast (no signer capability at all — enforced by a runtime tripwire and a unit test). A separate broadcast module replays only receipts whose ticket says PASS. A FAIL ticket is refused, logged, and never touches the chain. This module is also T07's safety harness.

2. How it works (the pipeline)
tasks.readme_markdown:
One lighthouse. Twenty-eight lamps.
This arm holds the sounding line — it tastes the water before the ship commits.

T08 · MEDIUM · 100 PTS · SKILLENGINE · ATLANTIC TESTNET (688689)

--- ## 1. What this is The Dry-Run Executor answers one question before any transaction is allowed near the chain: **what would happen if we sent this?** It simulates via `eth_call` + `estimateGas` — never broadcasting — and issues a signed-by-nobody **SimulationReceipt**: predicted PASS or FAIL, the exact revert reason on failure, the gas estimate with a **1.2× safety factor**, the predicted cost, and before/after state snapshots marked "chain unmodified". Execution is **structurally gated**: the dry-run module cannot broadcast (no signer capability at all — enforced by a runtime tripwire and a unit test). A separate broadcast module replays only receipts whose ticket says PASS. A FAIL ticket is refused, logged, and never touches the chain. This module is also T07's safety harness. ## 2. How it works (the pipeline) ``` proposed tx │ 1. VALIDATE address/sig sanity + chain-id MUST be Atlantic (688689), else REFUSED ▼ │ 2. eth_call `cast call` — surfaces the revert reason, zero broadcast ▼ │ 3. estimate `cast estimate` — success → gas number; failure → exact revert reason ▼ │ 4. gas price `cast gas-price` → predicted cost = ceil(estimate × 1.2) × price ▼ │ 5. project before/after state snapshots ("chain unmodified") ▼ SimulationReceipt JSON → PASS ticket → broadcast.py may replay it → FAIL ticket → broadcast.py REFUSES (exit 2, logged) ``` Revert decoding (`src/revert_decode.py`) handles `Error(string)`, `Panic(uint256)` (with the Solidity panic-code table), and custom errors — reported as selector hex, **never invented**. ## 3. Live proof (Atlantic testnet, real transactions) A purpose-built probe contract, `DryRunProbe`, was deployed at [`0xd5f956BCb0806BE66aEfa7C5559f195cd5224a8f`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/address/0xd5f956BCb0806BE66aEfa7C5559f195cd5224a8f) (deploy tx [`0xbb5fac…4748e44`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0xbb5facf81cd46d97cdb706ef2ecf6ecda70cd7cb32133b2ba5ed1a08b4748e44)). **Scenario A — dry-run predicts a REVERT.** `boom()` was dry-run: `cast estimate` failed with the exact reason **`DryRunProbe: forced boom`** (decoded from `Error(string)` payload `0x08c379a0…`). Receipt status: FAIL. The gate was then tested for real: `broadcast.py` was pointed at the FAIL ticket and **refused execution** (exit 2), appending to `runs/blocked-execution.log`. Nothing was broadcast — no transaction exists for `boom()`. **Scenario B — dry-run predicts SUCCESS, then the real broadcast matches.** `ping()` dry-run: PASS, estimate **58,219** gas → 1.2× limit **69,863** → predicted cost **0.00069863 PHRS**. A `forge script` simulation **without `--broadcast`** confirmed: "Script ran successfully / SIMULATION COMPLETE", script gas 62,804. The PASS ticket was then broadcast through the gate: tx [`0x639f87…012ee`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0x639f87ba9b79ce1a9c62ebe12fdb4753e021d2dfb7fa3caed0e48fab20b012ee) — **status success**, gas used **45,470** (within the 69,863 safety limit), `Pinged` event emitted, probe `count` moved **0 → 1** exactly as projected. **Scenario C — the prediction holds a SECOND time (repeatability).** A fresh `ping()` dry-run (receipt `runs/receipt-C.json`, block 31486270): PASS, estimate **37,379** → limit **44,855** → predicted cost **0.00044855 PHRS**. Broadcast through the gate: tx [`0xd294bb…4fb03`](https://atlantic.pharosscan.xyz/tx/0xd294bb5c03c55d7ffdd750b0a20384aa393e490da11fe3d7f67845d34d34fb03) — **status success**, gas used **28,370** (within the 44,855 limit), `Pinged` event with count **2** (was 1, exactly as projected). The gate was also re-tested against the fresh FAIL receipt → **refused** (exit 2) again. ### The prediction ledger — the executor keeps score One-shot proof is easy to cherry-pick, so the executor measures itself: every gated broadcast appends a prediction-vs-reality row to [`runs/prediction-ledger.jsonl`](runs/prediction-ledger.jsonl) (via `tools/ledger.py`, called automatically by `broadcast.py` after success). Two rows so far — **both predictions held** (status success, gas inside the 1.2× limit, state exactly as projected). The honest read: estimates **over-predict by ~30%** on Atlantic (58,219→45,470, 37,379→28,370); the 1.2× factor covers that drift with margin. Estimates are predictions — now with public drift data. Full logs: `runs/` · machine-readable: `evidence.json` · narrative: `evidence.md`. ## 4. Repository layout ``` tasks/t08-dry-run-executor/ ├── src/ │ ├── dryrun.py # the simulation gate (CANNOT broadcast — no signer capability) │ ├── revert_decode.py # Error/Panic/custom revert decoding, never invented │ └── broadcast.py # the ONLY broadcaster; replays PASS tickets via flock ├── tests/ │ └── test_estimation_parsing.py # 17 unit tests (parsing, decoding, gate math) ├── contracts/DryRunProbe.sol # on-chain probe (boom→revert, ping→success) ├── script/Probe.s.sol # forge script for the contract-flow dry-run ├── tools/rpc-normalize-proxy.py # local proxy: normalizes this RPC's strict params ├── runs/ # REAL run logs + SimulationReceipts (evidence) ├── foundry.toml ├── task.yaml REQUIREMENTS.md evidence.md evidence.json ├── REVIEWER_NOTES.md LINKS.md SUBMISSION.md VIDEO-GUIDE.md ``` ## 5. Run it yourself ```bash export PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH" cd tasks/t08-dry-run-executor set -a; source ../../.env; set +a # provides ATLANTIC_RPC_URL (never echoed) # 1) dry-run only — predicts, never broadcasts, no key needed python3 src/dryrun.py --rpc-url "$ATLANTIC_RPC_URL" \ --from 0xf76e6B0920e9332 …
